_comment: npm only honours `overrides` from the ROOT of an install tree, so a pack
cannot remediate advisories in its own transitive dependencies — the
entries below have to live in each consumer's package.json.
This file exists so that requirement is data rather than prose: a
consumer-side gate validator can read it and fail a module whose
overrides do not match, and the scaffolder can emit it for new packages.
Current entries are both reached through mocha, which has no released
version depending on fixed ranges (checked through 12.0.0-rc.6). Expect
this set to change as advisories are published and upstreams catch up —
it is living config, not a fixed list.
Verify with `npm audit --omit=dev` in a consumer after install: with these
entries the tree reports 0 vulnerabilities, without them 3.
